what: The Discount Calculator tells you how much you save on a sale and what you will really pay. Type the original price and the discount percent, and optionally your sales tax rate, to see the savings, the sale price and the final price with tax.
It helps shoppers check sale signs like "25% off", and helps sellers set sale prices. Adding tax shows the real amount you will pay at the checkout.
All maths happens in your browser as you type. Results are estimates and not financial advice.
uses: See the real price of an item marked with a percent off.
Add your sales tax to see the final amount you pay.
Try two prices and discounts to find the better deal.
Shop owners can see the new price after a planned discount.
Run the tool twice, using the first sale price as the new original price.
tutorial: Enter the full price before the sale in "Original price", for example 80.
Enter the percent off in "Discount (%)", for example 25. It must be between 0 and 100.
Type your rate in "Sales tax (%, optional)". Leave it empty to use 0, and the final price will equal the sale price.
"You save" is the amount taken off. "Price after discount" is the sale price. "Final price with tax" adds tax to the sale price.
Results update as you type, so you can quickly test a bigger or smaller discount.
features: You save = price × discount ÷ 100. Price after discount = price − savings.
Final price = sale price × (1 + tax ÷ 100), so tax is charged on the lower price.
Leave it empty if you do not pay sales tax or the price already includes it.
If the discount is below 0 or above 100, a message explains the problem.
No button needed; numbers change as you type.

example.title: Worked example: 25% off an 80 item
example.text: A pair of shoes costs 80 and is marked 25% off, and your sales tax is 8%. You save 80 × 25 ÷ 100 = 20.00, so the "Price after discount" is 60.00. The "Final price with tax" is 60 × 1.08 = 64.80. To stack an extra 10% off, type 60 as the original price and 10 as the discount: the new sale price is 54.00, which is a total saving of 32.5%, not 35%.

tips: Two discounts in a row are not added together; run the tool twice to get the right answer.
Leave the tax empty if the shelf price already includes tax, as with VAT in many countries.
A 100% discount gives a price of 0.
To find the discount percent from two prices, use the Percentage Calculator’s change section.
problems: It says the discount must be between 0 and 100 percent
You typed a discount below 0 or above 100. Enter a value in that range.
The final price is higher than the sale price
That is the tax. Clear the tax box if you do not want it added.
My stacked discount does not match the shop
Some shops apply coupons to the original price. Ask the shop how they apply them.
